caseno: Criminal Petition for Leave to Appeal No. 553 of 2011
lawyer:
Sharwardhi, Deputy Attorney General, instructed by Mrs. Sufia Khatun, Advocate-on-Record ------ For the Petitioner 
Ferozur Rahman, Advocate-on-Record ------ For the Respondent
parties:
The State, represented by the Deputy Commissioner, Narayangonj ------ Petitioner
Vs.
Mahmud Hassan alias Roni ------ Respondent
full_judgment:
Syed Mahmud Hossain J. This criminal petition for leave to appeal is directed against the judgment and order dated 24.11.2011 passed by a Division Bench of the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.10320 of 2009 making the Rule absolute. 

 3. On the basis of the First Information Report, Rupgonj Police Station Case No. 4 dated 06.10.2008, corresponding to G.R. No. 507 of 2008 under sections 302/201/ 34 of the Penal Code was started. 

 4. During investigation of the case, accused Sharif Ahammad Nayan was arrested and forwarded to the Chief Judicial Magistrate, Narayangonj. He made a confessional statement recorded under section 164 of the Code of Criminal Procedure implicating himself and other accused including the accused-respondent in the occurrence of causing death of the deceased and the accused-respondent was arrested. The accused-respondent filed applications for bail before the Judicial Magistrate and the then to Sessions Judge, Narayangonj, which were rejected. 

 6. After investigation of the case, police submitted charge sheet against eight accused including the accused-respondent, on the basis of which, the Judicial Magistrate concerned took cognizance of the offence against them. The case record was sent to the Court of Sessions Judge, Narayangonj where it was registered as Session Case No. 212 of 2011. The case was transferred to the learned Additional Sessions Judge, Second Court, Narayangonj for trial, who upon hearing an application filed by the Additional Public Prosecutor cancelled the bail of the accused-respondent relying upon a G.D. Entry filed by the informant and also upon allegations brought against him by his order dated 19.07.2011 and sent the accused-respondent   to custody. Then the Government sent the case to the Druto Bichar Tribunal No. 2, Dhaka, where the case was renumbered as Druto Bichar Tribunal Case No. 24 of 2011 now pending for trial. 

 7. After that, the accused respondent filed Miscellaneous Case No. 10320 of 2011 before the High Court Division and obtained Rule. The learned Judges of the High Court Division by their judgment and order dated 24.11.2011 made the Rule absolute and directed to enlarge the accused-respondent on bail. 

 9. Mr. Sharwardhi, learned Deputy Attorney General, appearing on behalf of the leave petitioner, submits that the accused-respondent having been released on bail granted by the High Court Division misused the privilege of hail by giving death threats to the informant and as such, the learned Additional Sessions Judge rightly cancelled the bail of the accused-respondent on relying upon a G.D. Entry made in that regard and as such, the High Court Division should have discharged the Rule. He further submits that the instant proceeding arose out of a sensational murder case and that in consideration of the gravity of the offence, the Government transferred the case to the Druto Bichar Tribunal No. 2, Dhaka and as such, the High Court Division should not have enlarged the accused-respondent on bail.
